title: What If Lake Baikal Vanished Overnight?

scenes.text: What if Lake Baikal vanished overnight? About one-fifth of Earth's fresh surface water would go with it.
It is nearly 400 miles long and more than a mile deep, the deepest lake on Earth.
It holds roughly 23,000 cubic kilometers of water. If every drop reached the ocean, the sea would rise only about six centimeters.
Its only outflow, the Angara River, would lose its source. The Angara feeds the Yenisei, which runs to the Arctic.
About two-thirds of Baikal's roughly 1,700 plant and animal species live nowhere else on Earth.
Baikal is the oldest freshwater lake on Earth, over twenty million years old. Gone in a night, it could not be rebuilt in ours.
